mainTopic: Doubts about חמץ after בדיקה: why a lenient assumption works for rabbinic בדיקת חמץ, and how the mouse-between-two-houses case compares to the משנה of שני שבילין (two paths, one טמא and one טהור)
overview: This amud opens at the end of a challenge from the previous amud. The גמרא had compared a doubtful חמץ case to two baskets of תרומה and חולין, where we are lenient, but the challenge says that works only for rabbinic תרומה. The גמרא answers that בדיקת חמץ itself is only rabbinic, since by Torah law ביטול is enough. It then goes through a series of mouse-and-חמץ cases and links each one to a known dispute. If the mouse went into one of two checked houses, it is like שני שבילין, and רבא (or רבי יוחנן) explains the dispute there between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי. If we are unsure whether the mouse went in at all, it is like the בקעה case, where רבי אליעזר and the חכמים disagree. If the mouse surely went in and a search found nothing, it follows רבי מאיר and the חכמים about a place with a חזקת טומאה. If the search found a piece, it follows רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about a lost grave that was found. Finally, leaving nine pieces and finding ten, or leaving ten and finding nine, follows רבי and the חכמים about found מעשר שני money.

steps.title: The leniency may work only for rabbinic תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge: the lenient assumption used for the baskets of תרומה may apply only because today's תרומה is rabbinic. Should it also apply to חמץ, which is a Torah prohibition?
steps.simpleTranslation: That leniency is said only about rabbinic תרומה. Do we really say it about חמץ, which is forbidden by Torah law?!
steps.whatsHappening: This line completes a challenge that began on the previous amud. The challenge argues that the comparison between the חמץ case and the baskets-of-תרומה case does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא compared a doubtful חמץ case to two baskets, one of תרומה and one of חולין. In that case we lean toward the lenient assumption. The challenge points out that today's תרומה is only דרבנן, and we are often lenient in rabbinic doubts. חמץ, however, is a דאורייתא prohibition, so maybe we cannot be lenient there.

keyTerms.meaning: Terumah that is obligatory only by rabbinic law (as it is nowadays)
Do we really say [this]?! (a challenging question)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'בתרומה דרבנן' finish the thought 'those words apply only to…' from the previous section. It is not a new topic.

phrases.english: [That applies only] to rabbinic teruma.
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence that started with 'הני מילי' a little earlier.

phrases.english: With regard to leavened bread, which is Torah law, do we say this?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge to the comparison made on the previous amud (חמץ compared to two baskets of תרומה and חולין).
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the doubtful חמץ case to the lenient ruling of the two baskets of תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The leniency may rest on the fact that the תרומה is only דרבנן. חמץ is דאורייתא, so the leniency should not carry over.

steps.title: Searching for חמץ is itself only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the question here is about בדיקה, which is a rabbinic obligation, because by Torah law ביטול alone is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the search for חמץ a Torah law? It is rabbinic! By Torah law, simply nullifying the חמץ is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. It explains that the issue here is the rabbinic duty to search, not the Torah prohibition of חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, a person fulfills his duty by doing ביטול, which means declaring his חמץ ownerless or worthless. The requirement to search the house is a rabbinic addition. Since the doubt is only about whether a house needs checking again, it is a doubt in a דרבנן matter, just like the תרומה case, so the comparison holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say…? (introduces a rhetorical rebuttal)
Nullification, declaring one's חמץ ownerless and worthless

steps.whatToRemember: By Torah law ביטול is enough. בדיקת חמץ is a rabbinic obligation, so doubts about the search can be treated like other rabbinic doubts.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, that בדיקה is דרבנן because ביטול suffices מדאורייתא, comes up again and again in the laws of פסח. It explains why we are sometimes lenient in doubts about searching.

phrases.english: Is that to say the search for leavened bread is Torah law?
It is rabbinic!
For by Torah law, mere nullification is sufficient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the nature of the obligation: the question is about rabbinic בדיקה, not the Torah prohibition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubt is about the Torah prohibition of חמץ, so no leniency is possible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubt is only about the rabbinic duty to search, since ביטול fulfills the Torah law. So the lenient תרומה model applies.

steps.title: A mouse takes חמץ, and two checked houses stand before it
steps.stepSummary: A new case: one pile of חמץ, two checked houses, and a mouse that took some חמץ into one of them, but we do not know which. The גמרא says this matches the case of שני שבילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is one pile of חמץ, and in front of it are two houses that were already checked. A mouse came and took some, and we don't know whether it went into this house or that house. This is the same as the case of the two paths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a new doubtful case and compares it to a known משנה about two paths. This step sets up the next move, where that משנה will be quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time both houses were already searched, so we cannot assume the חמץ went into an unchecked house. One of the two houses certainly now has חמץ, but each house on its own is only a doubt. The גמרא says this structure is just like the case of the two paths.

keyTerms.meaning: Two paths (a known case of doubtful impurity)

phrases.english: One pile of leavened bread
and before it two searched houses,
and a mouse came and took,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יָדְעִינַן אִי לְהַאי עָל אִי לְהַאי עָל —
phrases.english: and we do not know if it entered this one or that one —
this is the case of the two paths.

steps.triggerLanguage: צִבּוּר אֶחָד שֶׁל חָמֵץ וּלְפָנָיו שְׁנֵי בָתִּים בְּדוּקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case of one checked and one unchecked house to a new case where both houses were checked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubt about which of two checked houses received חמץ follows the same rules as the case of שני שבילין.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה of the two paths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: there are two paths, one טמא and one טהור. One person walked on one path and handled pure items, and another person walked on the other path and handled pure items.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: there are two paths, one impure and one pure. A person walked on one of them and then handled pure items. Then his friend came, walked on the second path, and also handled pure items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source it just mentioned, the משנה of the two paths. This step lays out that case before the rulings are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person on his own has a doubt about whether he walked on the impure path. Taken together, we know for sure that one of them became impure. This is exactly like the two houses, where one of them surely got חמץ but each one alone is only a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: He handled items that must stay ritually pure (e.g., תרומה)

phrases.english: As we learned: Two paths,
one impure and one pure,
and he walked on one of them and handled pure items,
and his fellow came and walked on the second,
and handled pure items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text for the comparison made in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The comparison of the two-houses mouse case to the case of the two paths.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about two paths, one טמא and one טהור (משנה טהרות).

steps.title: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי disagree about the two paths
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if they ask separately, both are טהור, and if they ask together, both are טמא. רבי יוסי says that either way both are טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If each one asked by himself, they are pure. If both asked at the same time, they are impure. רבי יוסי says: Either way, they are impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two opinions on how to rule for the two people. The timing of their question is the key point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, when each person comes alone, we judge him on his own and he keeps his חזקה of purity. When they come together, we cannot declare both pure, because one of them surely walked on the impure path. רבי יוסי rules them impure even when they ask separately.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked (a Sage for a ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not saying the facts change based on when they ask. The facts are the same. What changes is whether the Sage is forced to face the certainty that one of them is impure.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם נִשְׁאֲלוּ זֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: If this one asked by himself
and that one by himself — they are pure.
Both of them at the same time — they are impure.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסִי אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ טְמֵאִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: One way or another, they are impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם נִשְׁאֲלוּ זֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted משנה with its rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: asked separately they are טהורין, asked together they are טמאין. רבי יוסי: טמאין in all cases.

steps.title: רבא explains where both opinions agree
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רבי יוחנן) says that when they ask together, all agree both are טמא. When they ask one after the other, all agree both are טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say it was רבי יוחנן: If they asked at the same time, everyone agrees they are impure. If they asked one after the other, everyone agrees they are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא steps in to explain the dispute. He first narrows it by showing where רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי actually agree, which sets up the next step showing where they really disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, רבי יוסי seemed to rule טמא even when they asked separately. רבא says no: even רבי יוסי agrees that separate askers are טהור. This means the dispute must be about some middle case, which comes next.

phrases.english: Rava said, and some say it was Rabbi Yoḥanan:
At the same time — everyone agrees they are impure.

phrases.aramaic: בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.english: One after the other — everyone agrees they are pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reinterprets the dispute of step 5 by naming the cases where both sides agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Together: all agree טמאין. One after the other: all agree טהורין.

steps.title: The real dispute: one person asks about himself and his friend
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is only when one person comes and asks about both himself and his friend. רבי יוסי treats this like asking together, and רבי יהודה treats it like asking one after the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree only when one person comes to ask about himself and about his friend. רבי יוסי compares this to asking at the same time, and רבי יהודה compares it to asking one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his explanation by pinpointing the exact case of the dispute. This defines what the משנה's argument is really about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one person asks about both, the question raises both people at once, yet only one asker is physically present. רבי יוסי says the Sage still faces both cases together, so both are טמא. רבי יהודה says it counts as separate cases, so both are טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: About himself and about his fellow

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, asking together makes both טמא and asking separately makes both טהור, according to everyone. The argument is only about one person asking for both: רבי יוסי says this counts as together, and רבי יהודה says it counts as separate. The same pattern will apply to the two checked houses and the mouse.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of שני שבילין becomes the model for any case where one of two items is surely affected but each alone is only a doubt. The גמרא uses it here for the two checked houses.

phrases.english: They disagreed only
in one who comes to ask about himself and about his fellow.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְדַמֵּי לֵיהּ לְבַת אַחַת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei likens it to 'at the same time,'

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְדַמֵּי לֵיהּ לְזֶה אַחַר זֶה.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda likens it to 'one after the other.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בְּבָא לְהִשָּׁאֵל עָלָיו וְעַל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's explanation by identifying the one case in dispute.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי concerns only one person asking about himself and his fellow. רבי יוסי treats it as 'together' (טמאין), and רבי יהודה treats it as 'one after the other' (טהורין).

steps.title: Unsure if the mouse entered: like the valley case
steps.stepSummary: If we do not know whether the mouse entered the checked house at all, this is like the case of בקעה, which depends on the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is unclear whether the mouse went in or did not go in, this is the same as the 'valley' case, and it depends on the argument between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new kind of doubt: we are not sure whether the mouse with the חמץ went into the checked house at all. It says this matches a known case and sets up the next step, which quotes that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier steps, the doubt was about which house the mouse entered. Here the doubt is whether it entered at all. The גמרא connects this to a known מחלוקת so we can borrow its answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A valley or open field area

phrases.english: If it is uncertain whether it entered, uncertain whether it did not enter
phrases.notes: The mouse with the חמץ may or may not have gone into the checked house.

phrases.english: that is the case of the valley,
and it depends on the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָפֵק עָל, סָפֵק לָא עָל — הַיְינוּ בִּקְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new mouse-doubt case after the שני שבילין comparison is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubt about whether the mouse entered at all follows the בקעה dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבנן.

steps.title: The source: the person unsure if he entered the impure field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a person in a valley in the rainy season who is not sure he entered the field with טומאה. רבי אליעזר says he is טהור, and the חכמים say he is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: someone goes into a valley in the rainy season, and there is טומאה in a certain field. He says, 'I walked in that area, but I do not know if I went into that field or not.' רבי אליעזר says he is טהור, and the חכמים say he is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source it just mentioned, so we can see the dispute it is comparing to the mouse case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the rainy season, people may not walk in other people's fields, so the valley counts as a רשות היחיד. A doubt about טומאה in a רשות היחיד is usually treated as טמא. Here the person is not even sure he entered the field, and that is exactly what רבי אליעזר and the חכמים argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: A private domain; a doubt about טומאה there is treated strictly

steps.confusionAlert: The rain does not cause any טומאה. It only matters because in the rainy season nobody may walk in the fields, so the area counts as a רשות היחיד.

phrases.english: As we learned: One who enters a valley in the rainy season,
and there is impurity in a certain field,
and one person said: I walked in that place,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם נִכְנַסְתִּי בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׂדֶה
phrases.english: and I do not know whether I entered that field
or whether I did not enter.
Rabbi Eliezer deems him pure, and the Sages deem him impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source for the בקעה comparison made in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That a doubt about whether something entered at all is a known מחלוקת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה about entering a בקעה in the rainy season (טהרות).

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's reason: doubt about entering versus doubt about touching
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's rule: if the doubt is whether you entered the place, you are טהור. If you surely entered and the doubt is whether you touched the טומאה, you are טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי אליעזר used to say: If the doubt is about entering, he is טהור. If the doubt is about touching the טומאה, he is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אליעזר says טהור in the valley case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר splits the doubt into two levels. If you surely entered and only the touching is in doubt, the strict rule applies. If you are not even sure you entered, it does not. The חכמים treat both kinds of doubt the same, so they say טמא. Applied to the mouse: for רבי אליעזר, no new search is needed, and for the חכמים it is.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt about whether one entered the place
A doubt about whether one touched the טומאה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: a doubt about entering is טהור, and a doubt about touching is טמא. The חכמים are strict in both cases. So in the mouse case, if we are unsure the mouse entered, רבי אליעזר does not require a new search, but the חכמים do.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Eliezer would say:
An uncertainty about entry: he is pure;
an uncertainty about contact with impurity: he is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubt about entering is טהור, and a doubt about touching is טמא.

steps.title: The mouse surely entered, but the search found nothing
steps.stepSummary: If the mouse surely entered and we searched but found no חמץ, this depends on the מחלוקת of רבי מאיר and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the mouse did go in, and the person searched and did not find the חמץ, this depends on the argument between רבי מאיר and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case: we know for sure the mouse went in, but a search found nothing. It points to a known dispute and sets up the source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the doubt is no longer about entering. The question is whether a search that found nothing settles the matter, or whether we must keep worrying because the חמץ is surely somewhere.

phrases.english: If it entered, and he searched and did not find —
it is the dispute of Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from 'unsure if it entered' to 'surely entered, but nothing was found'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A search that found nothing after the mouse surely entered follows the dispute of רבי מאיר and רבנן.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: a known impurity stays until you find it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי מאיר: anything with a חזקת טומאה stays טמא until you know where the טומאה went.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי מאיר used to say: Anything that has a presumption of טומאה stays in its טומאה forever, until you find out where the טומאה is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source of רבי מאיר's view to explain the mouse case from step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, when we know טומאה was in a place, an empty search does not remove the presumption. We assume the search simply missed it. Applied to the mouse: since the mouse surely brought חמץ in, an empty search is not enough for רבי מאיר. The רבנן are more lenient once a proper search was done.

keyTerms.meaning: A presumption that something is impure

steps.whatToRemember: There are two different doubts. (1) Unsure if the mouse entered: this follows רבי אליעזר vs. the חכמים. (2) Surely entered, but nothing was found: this follows רבי מאיר vs. the רבנן, and רבי מאיר says the presumption stays until you find the חמץ.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a 'presumption' (חזקה) can outlast an empty search, which is a key idea for how much searching for חמץ is enough.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Meir would say:
Any thing that is in a presumption of impurity,
remains forever in its impurity

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּוָּדַע לָךְ הַטּוּמְאָה הֵיכָן הִיא.
phrases.english: until it becomes known to you where the impurity is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the רבי מאיר comparison made in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That an empty search does not remove a known presumption, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה quoting רבי מאיר on חזקת טומאה.

steps.title: The Rabbis' side: search all the way down to bedrock
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the משנה. The חכמים say you search until you reach bedrock or untouched earth. If you still find nothing, the טומאה is treated as gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: he keeps searching until he reaches rock or untouched (virgin) soil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה from the last step by giving the חכמים's opinion against רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said the place stays טמא until we know where the טומאה went. The חכמים say a full, deep search is enough: if nothing turns up, we treat it as gone. Applied to חמץ: if the mouse surely brought חמץ in and we searched well and found nothing, the חכמים would say the house is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Virgin soil, ground that was never dug, so no טומאה could be under it

steps.whatToRemember: Mouse surely entered, searched, found nothing: רבי מאיר says still a problem. חכמים say a thorough search is enough.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
He searches until he reaches
rock or virgin soil.
phrases.notes: Below this point, no טומאה could possibly be.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה begun in step 12 by giving the other side of the מחלוקת.
steps.raayaObject: The case where the mouse surely entered, we searched, and found nothing (step 11)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of רבי מאיר and חכמים about a place with a חזקת טומאה

steps.title: New case: the mouse entered, we searched, and found a piece of חמץ
steps.stepSummary: If the mouse went in and we searched and found a piece of חמץ, this matches the מחלוקת of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the mouse entered, and he searched and found a piece of חמץ, this is the dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new version of the mouse case and says which מחלוקת it depends on. This sets up the next step, where the source is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the search did find a piece of חמץ. But we do not know if it is the same piece the mouse brought in. Can we assume it is the same piece, or must we search the whole house?

phrases.english: If it (the mouse) entered, and he searched and found (a piece)
it is the dispute of רבי
and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from 'searched and found nothing' to a new case: 'searched and found something'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case where the mouse entered and a piece of חמץ was found depends on the מחלוקת of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: The lost grave that was later found
steps.stepSummary: There was a field with a lost grave, and later a grave was found there. רבי says it is the same grave, so the rest of the field is טהור. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the whole field must be searched.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: a field where a grave was lost makes anyone who enters it טמא. If a grave was found in it, whoever enters is טהור, because I say the grave that was lost is the grave that was found. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: the entire field must be searched.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that is the source for the מחלוקת it just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי assumes that what was found is what was lost, so we can stop worrying. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it might be a different grave, so the whole field must be checked. For חמץ: by רבי, the piece we found is the mouse's piece and we are done. By רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, we must search the whole house.

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave's exact spot was lost
'For I say', a reasoning formula that assumes the most likely explanation

steps.confusionAlert: Here the person entering a field with a lost grave is טמא, even though the בקעה case (step 9) made רבי אליעזר say טהור. The difference: in this field, there is surely a grave. The question is only where it is, not whether he entered the place of טומאה.

phrases.english: As it was taught: a field in which a grave was lost —
one who enters it is טמא.
If a grave was found in it —
one who enters it is טהור,
for I say: the grave that was lost
is the grave that was found —
these are the words of רבי.
רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
The entire field must be searched.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the מחלוקת named in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The case where the mouse entered and a piece of חמץ was found (step 14)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a field where a grave was lost and later found

steps.title: New case: he left nine pieces and found ten
steps.stepSummary: If someone left nine pieces of חמץ and later found ten, this matches the מחלוקת of רבי and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he left nine (pieces of חמץ) and found ten, it is the dispute between רבי and the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings yet another mouse case and names the matching מחלוקת. This sets up the source quoted in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Finding ten where he left nine shows that something changed: a mouse added at least one piece. The question is how to view the pile. Is it the original nine plus something new? Or was the original moved and replaced?

phrases.english: If he left nine and found ten —
it is the dispute of רבי and the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another variation of the mouse-and-חמץ problem, now about counting pieces.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case where he left nine and found ten depends on the מחלוקת of רבי and רבנן.

steps.title: He left one hundred and found two hundred: רבי's view
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא: someone left a מנה of מעשר שני money and found two hundred. רבי says it is חולין and מעשר שני mixed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: if he left a מנה (100 coins) and found two hundred, it is חולין and מעשר שני mixed with each other. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the ברייתא that is the source for the nine-and-ten case. This step gives only רבי's opinion. The חכמים's opposing opinion comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי assumes the original מעשר שני money is still there, and that extra money (treated as חולין) was added. So the pile is a mix, and we cannot tell which coins are which. Applied to חמץ: the original pieces are assumed still to be there, with something new added on top.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin amount equal to 100 דינרים
Second tithe, holy produce or money that must be eaten or spent in ירושלים

phrases.english: As it was taught: if he left a מנה (of מעשר שני)
and found two hundred,
חולין and מעשר שני
are mixed with each other —
these are the words of רבי.
phrases.notes: The רבנן's opposing view continues next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the מחלוקת named in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The case where he left nine pieces of חמץ and found ten (step 16)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about leaving a מנה of מעשר שני and finding two hundred

steps.title: The Sages say all the found money is ordinary
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא from step 17 ends with the חכמים, who say that all the money found is חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: it is all ordinary (non-holy) money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it started in step 17 by giving the opinion of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said the two hundred found are a mix of the original מעשר שני and extra חולין. The חכמים disagree. Since someone clearly touched this spot, he may have taken the original מנה and left different money, so none of it can be identified as the original מעשר שני. Applied to חמץ: the nine pieces left and ten found might all be different pieces, so the search must be redone.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with רבי

steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the parallel for the 'left nine, found ten' case of step 16. It shows why, according to the חכמים, the found חמץ cannot be assumed to be the same pieces that were left.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
It is all non-sacred money.
phrases.notes: Someone else was involved, so he may have taken the original מנה and left other money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 17 by giving the opposing view.
steps.raayaObject: The case of leaving nine pieces of חמץ and finding ten (step 16)
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: left a מנה of מעשר שני and found two hundred. The חכמים say it is all חולין.

steps.title: Left ten pieces and found nine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the reverse case, where fewer pieces of חמץ are found than were left, and says it matches the סיפא of the same ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he left ten pieces and found nine, this is the same as the latter part of the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the opposite case, where something is missing. It says the case matches the end of the same ברייתא, which it is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the problem was finding extra חמץ. Now one piece is missing. The גמרא does not give a new ruling here. It points to the סיפא of the ברייתא, so the same מחלוקת will decide this case too.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter part of a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: If he left ten and found nine
this is the latter clause,
phrases.notes: This refers to the end of the same ברייתא about מעשר שני money.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִנִּיחַ עֶשֶׂר וּמָצָא תֵּשַׁע הַיְינוּ סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the 'found more' case to the reverse 'found fewer' case, using the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving ten pieces of חמץ and finding nine depends on the same מחלוקת as the סיפא of the מעשר שני ברייתא.

steps.title: Left two hundred and found one hundred
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא of the ברייתא: someone left two hundred of מעשר שני money and found one מנה. רבי says one מנה is still here and one was taken. The חכמים say all of it is חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: if he left two hundred and found one hundred, one hundred is still lying here and one hundred was taken. These are the words of רבי. And the Sages say: it is all ordinary money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of the ברייתא to support the case of 'left ten, found nine.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי assumes the money that is here is part of the original, and only part was taken. So for חמץ, the nine are original and only one piece is missing. The חכמים assume that whoever took some of it took all of it, and this is different money. So for חמץ, none of the nine can be trusted as the original pieces, and the search must be redone.
steps.confusionAlert: מוּטָל here means 'taken away.' It does not mean 'lying there.' רבי is saying half the money stayed and half was removed.
steps.whatToRemember: Both cases follow one מחלוקת. רבי treats whatever is found as part of the original, so extra means a mix and missing means part was taken. The חכמים treat it all as new, so all of it is חולין and the חמץ search starts over.

phrases.english: As it was taught: if he left two hundred and found a maneh (one hundred) —
one maneh stayed in place and one maneh was taken,
phrases.notes: The money still here is part of the original מעשר שני.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi.
And the Sages say: it is all non-sacred money.
phrases.notes: Whoever took part of it took all of it, so this is different money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the סיפא that step 19 pointed to.
steps.raayaObject: The case of leaving ten pieces of חמץ and finding nine
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא סיפא: left two hundred of מעשר שני and found one מנה. רבי says one is still here and one was taken. The חכמים say all of it is חולין.
